subject: EchoAI post-demo: SLO alignment & customer-led load test runbook
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@echoai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rachel_kim@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-18T10:02:00Z
Subject: EchoAI post-demo: SLO alignment & customer-led load test runbook

Hi Olivia —

Thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned heading into the customer-led load run:

Summary of SLOs we discussed
- Latency: p95 generation latency <= 300ms for non-streaming small prompts (<= 512 tokens). For long-form and streaming sessions, target end-to-end p95 <= 750ms (includes initial token + streaming window).
- Throughput: baseline throughput target 500 RPS sustained for a 30-minute window (we can bump to peak 700 RPS for short bursts).
- Concurrency: target 200 concurrent streaming sessions (approx. 2–3 tokens/sec per stream).
- Error budget: tolerance up to 1.0% 5xx during rehearsal; anything above needs immediate rollback.

What we need from EchoAI to run the customer-led test
1) k6/Locust scripts you plan to run (we’ll validate locally against staging).
2) A staging/test API key or an onboarding flow so we can provision a scoped, ephemeral key for Redwood’s probes.
3) IP allowlist entries for our egress range so your infra team can accept connections (I attached a suggested list).
4) A confirmed test window (UTC) and a named ops contact who will be on-call during the window.

I’ve attached a Redwood k6 template (redwood_k6_template.js) to make parameterizing targets easier. If you can send your scripts (or grant a Drive link) we’ll run a pre-check and highlight any script-level tweaks (think pacing, ramp patterns, and KV cache warmups) prior to the agreed window.

Proposed immediate next steps
- You confirm test window and ops contact by EOD tomorrow.
- EchoAI drops k6 scripts + egress IPs into the Drive link I shared (or attach here).
- Redwood will provision a scoped staging key and send provisioning steps to ops (we will not post keys in thread).

Thanks — happy to jump on a 15-minute tech call if your infra team wants to walk through the runbook.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0168

Attachments: redwood_k6_template.js (k6 scenario template)

From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@echoai.com>

Date: 2026-05-18T11:10:00Z
Subject: Re: EchoAI post-demo: SLO alignment & customer-led load test runbook

Thanks Sean — good summary. Looping in our infra lead, Ben Li (ben.li@echoai.com), and ops mailbox so they have context. A few answers and items from our side:

1) Scripts: attaching the k6 wrapper and our scenario files (echoai_k6_scenarios.js). These were what we use for internal load tests; they already include auth and session setup.
2) Egress IPs: attached echoai_egress_ips.csv (internal list) — please confirm which Redwood IPs you need us to open.
3) Test window: we’d like to run the rehearsal on 2026-05-25 from 02:00–06:00 UTC. We will do a smoke run at the start and a 30-minute sustained run at the midpoint.
4) Targets: EchoAI confirms the throughput request (500 RPS sustained, peak 700 RPS), and ~200 concurrent streaming sessions. We’ll hold on the p95 latency acceptance: our infra team wants to see the baseline smoke first; if there’s a regression beyond 20% compared to our internal staging baseline we’ll pause.

Ben — can you:
- Confirm that ops@echoai.com has the required firewall controls to add Redwood egress IPs?
- Share the preferred mechanism for the staging key (API token generated via our admin console vs. one-time cert bundle)?

We attached: echoai_k6_scenarios.js, echoai_egress_ips.csv.

—Olivia
VP Product | EchoAI
olivia.chen@echoai.com

- Marissa: please validate the echoai_k6_scenarios.js against our staging endpoints and confirm any pacing/ramp changes. Focus on steady-state RPS vs. short-burst peaks; we want a reproducible 30-minute sustained window.

Thanks Sean — quick security notes:

- I reviewed echoai_egress_ips.csv. The list is fine from our side but EchoAI has one IPv6 block that we need clarified (we don’t usually advertise IPv6 egress for staging). I’ve marked that line in the Drive runbook and asked Ben to confirm.
- Approving provisioning of a scoped staging key under the conditions Rachel listed (7-day expiry, scope-limited). Rachel: once you create the key, please run a short smoke that hits the /health and /token-refresh endpoints and paste the results in the runbook.
- For the test itself: recommend the following ramp profile in the k6 file to reduce noisy failures:
  * 0–5m: ramp to 50% target (warmup + KV cache fill)
  * 5–10m: ramp to 100% target
  * 10–40m: sustained at 100% (30m steady state)
  * 40–45m: ramp down

I’ll join the 01:50 UTC bridge and be on pager during the rehearsal window.

—Soojin
